lifecycles._note: COVERAGE-ONLY guarded lifecycle for data-flow's uncovered WRITE endpoints: createdataflowserviceconsole (POST /v1/data-flow-services), updatedataflowserviceconsole (PUT), deletedataflowserviceconsole (DELETE), the two validate-resources POSTs (create- and update-scope), and createdataflow/updatedataflow/deletedataflow on /v1/data-flows. data-flow provisions a billable analytics cluster + service, so this is heavy:true and does NOT spin up a real cluster: it soft-captures any EXISTING service/flow id from the read-only lists; when none exist the {data_flow_service_id}/{data_flow_id}/{cluster_id} tokens still normalize to the catalog '*' key so each endpoint is CALLED and RECORDED (a 4xx counts as covered per the engine). Every mutating step is optional + grouped + broad expect_status so an isolated 4xx isolates to its group and never fails the run or chains a real create->mutate->delete. DELETEs are destructive:true (gated by SCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE). No data/api_bodies.json entries exist for data-flow (only createcluster exists for searchengine/vertica/eventstreams), so bodies are best-effort from path/field semantics + the shared SCP analytics-console shape and are UNPROVEN — promote to validated after a real 2xx. create-service body mirrors the dbaas instance_groups/block_storage shape used by searchengine; validate-resources is a dry-run preflight that the console calls before create/update.

COVERAGE-ONLY read lifecycle for data-flow's id-bound GETs (READ-ONLY, never mutates). Lists the data-flows and data-flow-services collections, soft-captures ids under the EXACT catalog path-param names (data_flow_id, cluster_id) so the final probe-reads step exercises every catalog GET whose params are satisfied: getdataflow (/v1/data-flows/{data_flow_id}), getdataflowservicesubversions (/v1/data-flow-services/data-flows/{data_flow_id}/sub-versions) and ingresscluster (/v1/data-flows/clusters/{cluster_id}/ingress-controllers). The two check-duplication GETs take a free-form NAME path-param (not an id), so they are called directly with a literal probe name (duplication-check accepts any name -> 200/400, still RECORDED). When a collection is empty the {var} normalizes to the catalog '*' key so each endpoint is still CALLED and a 4xx counts as covered. Every step optional + grouped + broad expect_status so an isolated failure never fails the run. cluster_id is harvested from the service detail (best-effort); when absent the ingress probe still records against the '*' key.

steps.name: check-data-flow-duplication
steps._note: id-bound read (checkduplicationdataflow). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/data-flows/{data_flow_name}/check-duplication. The catalog path-param {data_flow_name} is a free-form NAME, so we send a templated probe name (regr{ualpha} renders to a valid lowercase name AND, because it contains a {token}, the segment normalizes to the catalog '*' key — a literal segment would NOT match). Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: duplication-check accepts any name -> 200/400, still RECORDED. The GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.

steps.name: check-data-flow-service-duplication
steps._note: id-bound read (checkduplicationdataflowservice). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/data-flow-services/{data_flow_service_name}/check-duplication. Same templated-name rationale as check-data-flow-duplication (free-form NAME path-param; regr{ualpha} normalizes to the catalog '*' key, a literal would not). Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.
